long_biography.plain_text:
Centre Point made Harry John Hyams one of post-war London's most visible property developers. He assembled the St Giles site, negotiated a planning arrangement with London County Council and commissioned Richard Seifert's firm to create a sculptural high-rise. His insistence on a single blue-chip tenant left the building empty for years, making it both a landmark and a symbol of speculative development.

Hyams was equally methodical as a collector. Over half a century he filled Ramsbury Manor with paintings, ceramics, furniture, clocks and historic cars. His estate passed the manor and collections to the Capricorn Foundation, with instructions to conserve them and provide public access. The foundation now supports exhibitions and museum loans in his memory.
